A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Relocated material and corresponding results can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original multilabel classification and label-ranking experiments, including F1 scores, Kendall correlations, convergence curves, and learned log-partition evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds empirical comparisons with MCMC and min-max training methods.

M1.justification: The joint energy/log-partition objectives, Algorithm 1, Fenchel–Young extension, and model representations are retained. The added optimization and sampling procedures concern comparison methods, not changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six multilabel datasets, including Mediamill in Appendix A, and the same six label-ranking datasets. The added comparisons introduce no new task, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: V2 Tables 1–2 add evaluated Logistic (MCMC) and Logistic (min-max) comparators across both tasks. Exact MLE also joins the tabulated multilabel comparison, beyond its existing role in convergence plots. V1's GFY comparator is retained as Generalized Fenchel-Young.

E3.justification: The added baseline experiments introduce optimistic Adam with an MLP generator and REINFORCE, and Metropolis–Hastings with uniform proposals. Existing dataset splits, validation/refitting procedures, metrics, and Appendix A's convergence-run settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The prior-sample-count sensitivity curves in Figures 1 and 3, log-partition generalization evaluation in Figure 2, and architecture/loss comparisons in Appendix A are retained. The new benchmark comparator rows add no distinct ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores and learning curves without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added baseline rows follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial baseline results while retaining all matched earlier scores and plotted results. For example, Table 1 adds scene/unary-MLP F1 scores of 71.57 for MCMC and 52.54 for min-max alongside the unchanged logistic min-min score of 75.35. Table 2 adds authorship/Birkhoff-MLP Kendall scores of 89.68 and 78.50, respectively, alongside the retained 90.80.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 changes Lemma 2's proof justification from claiming it is a corollary of Lemma 1 to invoking classical conjugate calculus. This is a limited correction to the mathematical justification; the theorem statements, assumptions, and principal derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and principal conclusion retain the claims of joint energy/log-partition learning, MLE recovery in function space, MCMC-free optimization, log-partition generalization, and tractable sparsemax training.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 replaces a generic statement about difficult min-max optimization with an explanation involving high-variance REINFORCE gradients. Section 5 newly acknowledges that evaluation primarily concerns mode prediction and leaves conditional sampling and generative evaluation unresolved.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 adds implementation information for the new baselines: optimistic Adam, an MLP generator, REINFORCE, and uniform-proposal Metropolis–Hastings. Existing JAX information, dataset-access links, and documented convergence-experiment hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 2.7 explicitly relates log-partition optimization to Wang et al. (2018), Arbel et al. (2021), and Senetaire et al. (2025), distinguishing the paper's conditional neural formulation, guarantees, and loss generalization. This substantially clarifies positioning around the central idea. V2 also adds discrete score-matching, NCE, and neural-transport references and removes the Hopfield comparison.

P1.justification: V2 adds subsection 2.7, extends and retitles the conclusion, makes localized explanatory and terminology edits, updates correspondence/publication text, and removes Author contributions. The main section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V1's appendix Table 3 becomes expanded main-text Table 1, and its ranking Table 1 becomes expanded Table 2, with additional method blocks and separators. Appendix tables reflow, and Figure 3's caption replaces incorrect panel references with column references. All three plotted figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens comparative evidence through Tables 1–2 and improves transparency through the direct related-work discussion in Section 2.7 and the sampling limitation in Section 5. These are useful improvements to the existing paper, although missing sampler-budget details and repeated-run uncertainty limit the strength of the new empirical comparisons.
